answer: One defense binds each agent to a unique, non-shareable storage commitment. At join, a node is seeded a large random region — its karst — honeycombed with cells it must retain. The protocol fires surprise retrieval audits, each demanding a specific cell plus a pigment-like fingerprint hash proving the bytes are its own, not borrowed. A sybil ring cannot pour one cache across many masks any more than a single dune anchors a hundred roots: each fake must provision its own independent terabytes, continuously, so attack cost scales linearly in real storage, not one mint cloned.
